verdict.root_cause: Cart stopped accepting connections at ~20:11–20:12, about a minute after platform-automation re-applied the 2.2.0-cart-hotfix.2 image reference to cart at 20:11:36 [tr_04f673f444a3]. frontend's only errors in the window are client-side gRPC transport failures dialing cart at 172.18.0.19:7070 — dial i/o timeouts near 20:12 escalating to host-unreachable with no connection ever established by 20:15:41 [tr_1fa4a1dbfeac] — the signature of a container that is no longer running. checkout, which calls cart on the PlaceOrder path, moves from a flat-zero error ratio over 32 baseline samples to intermittent errors first crossing at 20:13 [tr_4a0878a49e1e], while its pre-incident traces show cart and all other dependencies healthy in single-digit milliseconds [tr_9b5a1302dfd3], and checkout itself has no recorded change [tr_080fa64db1c4]. The failing mechanism is the artifact now deployed on cart.
verdict.reasoning: frontend's log lines are propagated downstream transport errors naming a single resolved IP:port identified as the cart call in checkout, with frontend-internal bugs, DNS, TLS/auth and application-level cart errors each excluded [tr_1fa4a1dbfeac] — so frontend and checkout are noticers, not culprits. Cart's only temporally adjacent change is the 20:11:36 image update, the earlier flapping having ended ~10.7h prior [tr_04f673f444a3], and onset in checkout (20:13) and frontend (20:12:18) follows it by about a minute [tr_4a0878a49e1e, tr_1fa4a1dbfeac]. Failure at TCP connect means nothing is answering on cart's socket, which excludes process_freeze (whose socket still accepts). Checkout's partial, spiky error ratio fits only cart-touching paths failing [tr_f945f892d2b9]. Checkout's empty log stream is uniformly empty back through baseline and therefore a pipeline gap, not a signal [tr_b7763f45ca3a].
open_questions: No dispatch queried cart directly — its logs, container state and restart counts were never retrieved, so the deploy-to-failure link is inferred entirely from caller-side evidence plus a change record.

The applied tag is the same one rolled forward and back five times earlier that day [tr_04f673f444a3]; the underlying digest is unknown, and whether cart failed to start or was cut off at the network layer is unsettled since host-unreachable fits both.
No per-dependency error breakdown exists for checkout [tr_4a0878a49e1e, tr_f945f892d2b9], and 9 of the 13 blast-radius services were never examined.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart is running normally but severed from the pod network, so callers' dials time out and then report host-unreachable.
alternatives.why_not: Explains caller symptoms equally well, but nothing ties a connectivity loss to an image update on that same service a minute earlier; the distinguishing signal — cart's own log complaining it cannot reach anything — was never collected.

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix image on cart is repeatedly killed for exceeding a memory or connection limit, so its socket disappears intermittently.
alternatives.why_not: No cart-side resource telemetry was gathered at all, and the escalation from timeout to steady host-unreachable by 20:17 looks like a sustained absence rather than the flapping a kill-loop would produce.

proposal.expected_effect: Cart accepts TCP connections on :7070 again. Observable two ways: frontend's gRPC client errors naming 172.18.0.19:7070 (dial i/o timeout, then host-unreachable, currently several per second) cease entirely; and checkout's span error ratio returns to the flat zero it held over 32 baseline samples before 20:13, allowing one 5m rate window to drain. A brief burst of resets during container recreate is expected and is not failure.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, ~7 minutes after recreate, frontend still logs host-unreachable to 172.18.0.19:7070 and checkout's error ratio stays non-zero. That would mean the artifact is not the mechanism — cart may be running but detached at the network layer (no one ever queried cart's container state, logs, or restart count), or the 20:11:36 record's prior image is literally 'None' so the rollback redeployed the same digest. Neither is fixable by an available action (reconnect_service is unavailable); next step is querying cart directly, not acting again.
proposal.risk: If cart was healthy and the break is network-level, this discards a working container's cache for nothing. The hotfix tag may have been fixing a real defect, which the rollback reintroduces; the tag has flapped five times today, so the prior tag is not known-good, and platform-automation may re-apply the hotfix within minutes and undo this. Chosen over restart_service because the evidence names a change, not process state, and because it is reversible.
proposal.blast_radius: cart directly; its inbound callers see resets during recreate — checkout on the PlaceOrder path and frontend on cart retrieval, hence frontend-proxy and load-generator user journeys. No other service's dependencies move.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical, simultaneous alerts across checkout, frontend, and the proxy with load-generator following cannot be dismissed, and no open incident covers them. The shared-path pattern hints at a downstream dependency of checkout/frontend, but that is only a prior for ordering dispatches.
